questions: Baclofen is a *GABA-B:Which inhibitory receptor subtype does baclofen activate?* receptor agonist that reduces spasticity by inhibiting spinal interneuron excitability.
Tizanidine is a central *α2:Which adrenergic receptor subtype has a central inhibitory role?* adrenergic agonist that suppresses polysynaptic reflex pathways in the spinal cord.
Dantrolene blocks the *ryanodine:Which SR calcium release channel is the target of dantrolene?* receptor on the sarcoplasmic reticulum to halt uncontrolled calcium release.

The life-threatening indication for intravenous dantrolene is *malignant hyperthermia:Which anaesthetic emergency is caused by uncontrolled RyR1-mediated Ca²⁺ release?* triggered by volatile anaesthetics or succinylcholine.
Abrupt withdrawal of intrathecal baclofen can precipitate life-threatening *seizures:What dangerous neurological complication results from sudden GABA-B agonist withdrawal?* and rhabdomyolysis.
